name: gap_continuation_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, the first 5 minutes (09:15-09:20) on a gap day acts as a price discovery containment window: counter-trend traders post limit sell orders at the opening high, creating a visible supply shelf (ORH). When a 5-second bar closes above the ORH on a gap-up day — with EMA(5-min) above EMA(13-min) confirming sustained directional pressure — it signals that all counter-trend supply at the shelf has been absorbed. The order book immediately above the ORH is thin because no participants pre-positioned limit offers there overnight; institutional TWAP programs fill at-market into this vacuum, driving NIFTY 15-25 spot points cleanly in the gap direction within the next 30-90 seconds before fresh supply emerges.

indicators.name: gap_pct
indicators.purpose: Day-level gap detection. Threshold 0.3% (0.003 fractional) — NIFTY's intraday daily range is ~0.8-1.2%, so a 0.3% overnight gap represents a meaningful global information signal without requiring an extreme macro event. Not scaled from the original's 0.5% equity threshold; NIFTY is smoother and less gappy than individual stocks, so a lower threshold captures the same economic signal (genuine institutional pre-positioning overnight).

indicators.name: orh
indicators.purpose: Opening range high: highest high of the first 5 minutes (09:15-09:20, 60 bars at 5s). This is a FIXED TIME WINDOW — 5 minutes regardless of bar size. Same time window as the original's '5-min opening range' concept. The ORH is the supply shelf that counter-trend traders defend; a close above it is the trigger.

indicators.name: orl
indicators.purpose: Opening range low: lowest low of the first 5 minutes. SAME FIXED TIME WINDOW as ORH. The ORL is the demand shelf on gap-down days; a close below it triggers the bearish signal.

indicators.name: ema_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute EMA (60 bars × 5s = 5 min), equivalent to the original's EMA(5) on 1-min bars. This is a TRADE TRIGGER — must be above EMA_156 to confirm the bullish trend is active. The 5-min EMA is the fastest meaningful trend line at our hold time (30-90s); shorter EMAs (12-24 bars) are too noisy at 5s frequency.

indicators.name: ema_156
indicators.purpose: 13-minute EMA (156 bars × 5s = 13 min), equivalent to the original's EMA(13) on 1-min bars. This is a CONTEXT FILTER — when EMA_60 > EMA_156 we are in a bullish micro-trend that makes gap continuation more probable. Same time horizon as original, different bar count. Not compressed further because the 13-min context window is already short and aligns with our gap observation window (first ~20 minutes of session).

indicators.name: close_strength
indicators.purpose: Fraction of bar range occupied by close (0=low, 1=high). Threshold >0.7 for longs (<0.3 for shorts). Equivalent to the original's 'breakout bar closes in upper 30% of its range' confirmation. At 5-second bars this is weaker signal than at 1-min, but it filters out wicks — a 5s bar that breaks ORH but closes near the bar's low indicates a false breakout or thin market, not institutional absorption.

conditions: close > orh (5s bar closes above opening range high)
ema_60 > ema_156 (5-min EMA above 13-min EMA: bullish alignment)
close_strength > 0.70 (bar closes in upper 30% of its range: no wick rejection)
VIX between 13 and 25 (some volatility for continuation, not chaotic)
time_minutes in [560, 615) (09:20-10:15 IST: gap momentum window only)
buy_ce.confirmation: All conditions simultaneously true on a single 5s bar

conditions: close < orl (5s bar closes below opening range low)
ema_60 < ema_156 (5-min EMA below 13-min EMA: bearish alignment)
close_strength < 0.30 (bar closes in lower 30% of its range: no wick bounce)
buy_pe.confirmation: All conditions simultaneously true on a single 5s bar

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option pts = ~8 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5. An ORH breakout should not retrace back inside the opening range (typically 8-15 spot pts wide on gap days); if NIFTY reverses 8 spot pts post-breakout, the supply shelf has reasserted itself and the institutional absorption thesis is false — exit before the throwback deepens.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option pts = ~14 NIFTY spot pts. First-leg gap continuation after ORH breakout on NIFTY averages 20-30 spot pts within 60-90s; targeting 14 pts (50% of expected move) gives 1:1.75 R:R and exits comfortably before the 09:30 profit-taking wave that typically compresses the continuation.
exit.eod_rule: flatten at 10:15 IST (no new entries beyond morning gap momentum window)

filters.vix_filter: VIX 13-25: below 13 means too calm (gaps don't continue — they fill immediately); above 25 means chaotic (gap reversals dominate, continuation unreliable)
filters.time_filter: 09:20-10:15 IST only; gap and go momentum is a first-hour phenomenon driven by overnight order overhang being worked off
filters.volume_filter: implicit in EMA alignment — sustained institutional buying lifts all timeframe EMAs; explicit volume filter not used as NIFTY index volume at 5s is noisy
filters.trend_filter: EMA_60 > EMA_156 for longs (opposite for shorts); gap direction IS the macro trend, EMAs confirm micro-trend alignment
filters.spread_filter: not applicable; limit order execution at candle close prices, no bid-ask spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — ORH breakout signals are observable and front-runnable by HFT, but at 5-second bar resolution the entry timing already absorbs the first microsecond of the move; institutional TWAP programs fill over multiple minutes so the 30-90s trade captures mid-order-flow, not the HFT spike

adaptation_notes: Original: NIFTY 50 and Next 50 stocks, 1-min bars, gap >0.5%, 5-min ORH/ORL breakout with volume_surge >2x, EMA(5)/EMA(13) alignment, bar close strength >upper 30%, hold 15-60 min. Key changes: (1) Universe: individual stocks → NIFTY index; relative_strength filter (stock gap vs index gap) eliminated — not applicable on the index itself. (2) Gap threshold: 0.5% equity → 0.3% NIFTY; indices are 4-5x smoother than individual stocks, so 0.3% represents the same signal strength economically. (3) Volume surge filter (2x average 5-min volume): eliminated for NIFTY because index volume at 5s is an aggregate proxy and noisy; EMA alignment provides equivalent trend confirmation. (4) EMA periods: EMA(5) and EMA(13) on 1-min → EMA(60) and EMA(156) on 5s — exact same clock time, different bar count. (5) Hold time: 15-60 min → 30-90 seconds; we trade the first micro-continuation burst of the gap, not the full intraday trend. (6) Session window: 09:15-12:00 → 09:20-10:15 IST — tighter because at 5s frequency the relevant microstructure signal (ORH breakout with thin order book) is strongest in the first 60 minutes only.
weaknesses: Gap days with ORH breakout conditions occur on ~20-30% of trading days; many days generate zero trades
Opening range on gap-up days is sometimes very wide (>20 spot pts on high-vol days), making ORH breakout entries occur far from fair value with extended risk

close_strength filter (upper 30% of bar range) is weaker at 5s than at 1-min because 5s bars have more noise and spread; a bar may have a strong close due to a thin single tick, not genuine absorption
EMA_60/EMA_156 may lag on fast-moving gap mornings, causing delayed alignment confirmation and missed entries
